name: influenza-crossparadigm
title: Influenza cross-paradigm — one Sego 2022 blueprint, three mechanical substrates
description:
This investigation is the capstone of the `viva-multicell-blueprint` build: it
ties together the backend-neutral blueprint (Task 17), the `compile(blueprint,
backend)` compiler (Task 13), both real backends running the full model (fields
Task 6, rules Task 7, systemic ODE fed live by CellCountStep Task 21, immune
recruitment via latent-pool activation Task 20, real footprints Task 19), the
comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare` — identity, raster, metrics)
and the three interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**Blueprint update.** The recruitment design (Task 20) activates a PRE-PLACED
LATENT immune pool, so the Sego blueprint's `initial_state` now pre-places 12
size-25 latent immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via
`extra_blocks`; the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so the
latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Runnable artifact.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.sego.sego_crossparadigm`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the
baseline composite for every study and drives the dashboard Composite Explorer.

**Reduced scale.** Every study runs at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs actually complete; this is a
demonstration, not paper scale. The comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Third paradigm (center-based).** A third mechanical substrate — a center-based
model (viva-munk / pymunk: each cell a circular rigid body, area-matched to the
blueprint `size`) — is now compiled from the SAME canonical blueprint via
`local:MunkBackend`, visualized as a third panel in every spatial playback, and
scored PAIRWISE (cpm↔vertex, cpm↔munk, vertex↔munk) in the equivalence and
counterfactual studies. It is deliberately NOT calibrated to the other two
(docs/mechanics.md §3), so it is a genuinely independent representation.

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the backends to agree.
Honest divergence is reported.

at_a_glance.role: §9.1, REVISED 2026-10-28. Both substrates' mechanics are defined term by term (docs/mechanics.md). Area stiffness and adhesion ratios are energy-matched; the tension scale (1.74), immune motility and the saturating chemotactic drift are CALIBRATED to the CPM (area 22.8/23.0, immune displacement 9.4/9.4 um) under a hard no-fold constraint. Epithelial wandering is NOT matched: the CPM-matching motility folds the vertex mesh, so the vertex epithelium wanders ~5x less (MSD 2.0 vs 9.5 um^2), though it exchanges neighbours (T1s).

§9.2, REVISED 2026-10-28. CPM exact (centroid RMS 0.000 um). The vertex model has one polygon per Sego cell: a connected sheet of 36 regular hexagons at area 25 plus 12 immune overlay islands, with no guard / medium polygons (was 50). Epithelial residual is sub-cell (RMS 1.60 um, max 2.44 um). 48/48 type match.

§9.3 CAPSTONE, re-run on the revised vertex substrate with mechanics-stochastic replicates. Fate (cross 0.938 between same-backend 0.926 / 0.944), occupancy IoU (0.135 between 0.100 / 0.175) and patch location (3.6 vs 3.3 um) are inside seed noise, so we fail to reject; the old IoU candidate signal does not survive. Remaining candidate: the vertex I-count leaves the narrow CPM 3-seed envelope at 45% of steps by N=400.

§9 stretch. Sweep initial viral load over seeds; both substrates agree on the STRICT DIRECTION -- the highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest on every backend and seed (CPM 1->7 / 1->2, vertex 1->7 / 1->6). Directional, not a dose-response curve.

HARDENING, re-run 2026-10-28. Fate is EQUIVALENT (run-cluster CI [-0.003, +0.001] within +/-0.05). The exact-position gap shrank from 0.92 to 0.135 (cross 0.472 vs same 0.608, CI [0.071, 0.210]): still not equivalent at +/-0.10. The old gap was mostly a degenerate null (identical mechanics across replicates) plus non-moving vertex cells; the rest tracks the less fluid vertex epithelium.

HARDENING / positive control, re-run 2026-10-28. The spatial TOST still REJECTS (cross 0.417 vs same 0.775), so the test has power. The earlier mechanism (vertex climbing the gradient) was an uncalibrated-chemotaxis artifact and is retired; the remaining divergence is positional / sorting and not yet isolated.

glossary.definition: Running the same model on two different mechanical substrates (CPM voxel vs vertex polygon) and comparing.
Pre-placed resting immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margin that recruitment activates in place (type switch), rather than inserting new topology.
Fraction of the t0 cohort in the same state (type, or alive-vs-dead) at each step across the two backends.
Intersection-over-union of the two backends' rasterized cell footprints (CPM voxel occupancy vs vertex face polygons).

question: Can ONE backend-neutral blueprint express the whole Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) and run it faithfully on three different mechanical substrates — a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm), a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue), and a center-based model (viva-munk) — and where do the substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live?
hypothesis: Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / latent-pool recruitment mechanism is compiled BYTE-FOR-BYTE identically onto all three backends and only the single mechanics node differs, cell-FATE dynamics should be nearly backend-independent, while SPATIAL morphology should diverge — each substrate samples the shared field at its own cell centroid and measures cell-cell contact through its own geometry. Divergence is therefore expected and is a finding about the substrate, not a bug. (Confirmed three-way: fate agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT across all three paradigm pairs, while spatial agreement is not — and the center-based model, which is not calibrated to the other two, is the most spatially divergent of the three.)

acceptance_criteria.behavior: Both substrates' mechanics are defined with per-type / per-pair parameters, and the vertex knobs without a CPM counterpart are calibrated to CPM area, motility and chemotactic drift (with non-identifiable ones reported as such).
Both backends reproduce the t=0 centroids/sizes/types; every vertex polygon is one blueprint cell (hexagonal sheet + immune overlay, no guard / medium faces) and the residual is reported.

The full Sego blueprint runs on BOTH backends at reduced scale; per-cell agreement, dynamics-with-band, and spatial-pattern + occupancy IoU are all computed, the three figures render under the inline cap, and the agree/diverge result is reported honestly.
Both backends agree on the monotone direction of infection vs initial viral load.

Under replication (6x6 seed grid), cross-backend fate agreement is TOST- equivalent to the same-backend baseline within ±0.05; the spatial (exact- position) result is reported with its representation caveat.

In a mechanics-dominated regime the spatial equivalence TOST REJECTS, and the migration-direction difference (vertex climbs the gradient, CPM does not) is the mechanistic cause — demonstrating the test has power.

executive.what_is_this: The capstone cross-paradigm demonstration: one backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint, compiled and run on both a Cellular Potts and a vertex substrate, with a full three-family comparison and three interactive figures.
executive.verdict: UPDATED per the 2026-10-28 vertex-mechanics review (feedback-response.md, second section). The vertex substrate was rebuilt: one polygon per Sego cell on a hexagonal sheet, immune overlay, fields overlaid not meshed, auto_reconnect, per-pair tension, stable sub-stepped integration, domain walls, and motility / chemotaxis calibrated to the CPM under a hard no-fold constraint. Its mechanics are defined in docs/mechanics.md. Vertex cells now move within the tissue and exchange neighbours, but the epithelium wanders ~5x less than the CPM's: the CPM-matching motility folds the vertex mesh. Replicates are now mechanics-stochastic on both backends. Fate stays equivalent. The exact-position gap fell from 0.92 to 0.135 (still not equivalent at +/-0.10). In the capstone, fate, occupancy and location are within seed noise; late I-count dynamics are the remaining candidate. The counterfactual still rejects, but its migration mechanism was an artifact and is retired. --- 2026-10-27 framing (still in force): REFRAMED per the 2026-10-27 review (see feedback-response.md). The contribution is a declarative, backend-neutral BLUEPRINT with auditable lowering to CPM and vertex — organized around three DISTINCT claims: (1) blueprint fidelity, (2) model portability, (3) scientific equivalence. Cross-backend agreement is Claim 3 evidence, NOT the headline, and never implies (1) or biological validity. Status by claim: (1) PARTIAL — t0 centroid/ID/type identity shown; area/footprint/ contact/adjacency/topology/round-trip not yet tested (Stage 2). (2) PARTIAL — one blueprint compiles to both with a byte-shared mechanism, but V/L/C/F producers are absent and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation (named deviations, so "Sego model with deviations", NOT "FULL Sego"; Stage 4). (3) SCOPED — on cell FATE the backends are equivalent under a DEPENDENCE-AWARE reanalysis (run-cluster bootstrap over the 6x6 grid: Δ -0.0015, 90% CI [-0.003,+0.001], within a ±0.05 margin that is NOT yet biologically justified); exact POSITION is not equivalent (a candidate representation effect, not yet causally isolated); the mechanics- dominated counterfactual shows the test has power. The earlier pair-level p=5.6e-36 overstated significance (dependent seed-pairs) and is retired. --- Prior reduced-scale reading (superseded as the headline, kept for provenance): Judged against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread), on cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread, so we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate effect at this scale and seed count (a null result, NOT proof of equality): cross-backend fate agreement 0.942 (N=400), within the same-backend baselines (CPM 0.934, vertex 0.943; equal 0.987 at CI scale); patch location 6.1 um cross vs 5.4 um same-backend; vertex trajectory inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 100% of steps. Final cell areas match (24.7 vs 24.5), so the spatial comparison is not representation-confounded. The ONE exception: raw infected-patch occupancy IoU trends ~25-35% below BOTH same-backend baselines (0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212) — flagged as a candidate weak substrate signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds, not attributed to seed noise without evidence. Dose-response direction is strict on both backends across seeds. Initial-state fidelity is exact on CPM and a clean 1:1 on vertex; the adhesion J<->tension mapping is directional. The earlier "fate agrees, morphology diverges" reading was an artifact of comparing a single seed-pair to zero. This is preliminary (reduced scale): the headline N=400 numbers use 3 CPM x 3 vertex seeds (9 cross pairs), and the vertex side is near-degenerate across seeds at this scale (the slow epidemic gives ~identical vertex I-counts; vertex-vs-vertex sd 0.006), so more vertex seeds barely move the result; the lighter CI test uses CPM {0,1,2} vs vertex seed 0. A substrate effect could emerge at larger scale, where the vertex seeds would no longer be degenerate. Known limits: the recruitment latent-pool approximation (T20-RECRUIT), the reduced scale, the producer-less ODE inputs V/L/C/F (Task 21), and the directional adhesion calibration.
decisions_needed: STAGE 1 (BP-01): formalize a versioned blueprint schema + canonical IR, separate from backend geometric init (units, coord frame, boundaries, tessellation-independent IDs, footprints, fields, contacts, latent states, seeds, init order, mechanism bindings, provenance, allowable loss).

STAGE 2 (BP-02/BP-04, extend initial-state-fidelity): prove blueprint fidelity beyond centroids/IDs — area, footprint, contact, adjacency, boundary, topology, round-trip, with explicit error measures and loss reports.

STAGE 3 (BP-07): adhesion-calibration now calibrates the vertex tension scale, immune motility and chemotaxis to CPM observables under a no-fold constraint (2026-10-28). Open: the vertex epithelium cannot reach CPM fluidity without folding (MSD 2.0 vs 9.5 um^2) -- needs a fold-aware topology handler or a softer epithelium; area dispersion unmatched; tension scale geometry-dependent (1.74 vs ~4); one cell size.

STAGE 4 (BP-05): V/L/C/F inputs have no producer and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation — build a producer/consumer ledger, implement or clearly designate deviations, and ablate frozen inputs.

STAGE 4 (BP-06): the ±0.05 fate-equivalence margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the dependence-aware reanalysis is done (cluster bootstrap) but power under biologically meaningful perturbations is not established.

STAGE 4 (BP-08): biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is NOT validated — digitize figure/table/parameter anchors and compare predictive intervals on held-out data; no biology inferred from cross-backend agreement.
STAGE 4 (dose-response redefine): separate virion inoculum from seeded infected fraction; 6-10 graded doses x replicate seeds; it is currently directional-only, NOT a dose-response curve.
STAGE 5 (BP-09): compile a SECOND independent tissue blueprint through the same schema with no influenza-specific adaptations — the decisive generality test.

competing_frameworks.name: Cellular Potts (CPM / viva-cpm)
competing_frameworks.description: Lattice model: cells are voxel sets evolving by Metropolis acceptance of pixel copies under a Hamiltonian (volume, contact J, chemotaxis). Sorting and motility emerge from energy minimisation on the lattice.

competing_frameworks.name: Vertex model (tyssue / vivatyssue)
competing_frameworks.description: Polygon model: the epithelium is a confluent hexagonal sheet of faces with shared edges, evolving by overdamped force balance (area elasticity, per-type-pair junction tension, active motility + saturating chemotaxis via ActiveMigration) with T1/T3 neighbour exchange (auto_reconnect). Immune cells are an overlay layer (Sego's z=1 over z=0), and fields are overlaid on the tissue. Equations: docs/mechanics.md.

competing_frameworks.name: Framing
competing_frameworks.description: The investigation's question is whether a single backend-neutral blueprint gives the SAME scientific answer on these two competing substrates. Equivalence (crossparadigm-equivalence) and its adversarial positive control (substrate-divergence-counterfactual) together bound WHEN the frameworks agree (shared-mechanism-driven fate) and WHEN they diverge (mechanics-driven position).

studies.name: adhesion-calibration
studies.question: Are the two substrates' mechanics defined and parameterized so that they are mechanically comparable -- per cell type and per type pair -- and which vertex parameters are fixed by the CPM, which must be calibrated, and which cannot be?

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED (2026-10-28): the earlier "tension non-identifiable" result came from the vertex backend collapsing the per-pair table to one mean tension and running only 6 steps.

evidence.observed: earlier: CPM mean 23.6 / CV 0.098; vertex mean 34.9 / CV 0.064; CV spread < 0.01 across scale

findings.explanation: Only the mean tension reached the mesh; the Voronoi tessellation set the area.

findings.statement: With the mechanics defined and per-pair tension applied, the vertex tension scale, immune motility and chemotactic mobility are identifiable and calibrated to the CPM (area 22.8/23.0, immune displacement 9.4/9.4 um, drift within ~10% for g >= 0.003). Epithelial wandering is capped by mesh validity (MSD 2.0 vs 9.5 um^2), and area dispersion is unmatched.
findings.explanation: Tension contracts cells against area elasticity; active motility replaces the CPM temperature's wandering, up to the shear a tyssue sheet tolerates without folding.
findings.next_action: a fold-aware topology handler (or a softer epithelium) to reach CPM fluidity; validate on a second geometry / cell size (BP-07)

studies.claim: RE-CALIBRATED 2026-11-05 for the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (immune cells are half-size polygons in the sheet; reconnect p_4 = 1, T1 at 0.2 x side). Tension scale 1.683 (area 22.97 vs CPM 22.98). Both motilities are fold-free CAPS: epithelium 26.6 (MSD 2.2 vs CPM 9.5 um^2; fit 81), in-sheet immune 56.1 (displacement 4.6 vs 9.4 um; fit 214). Tension noise 5 (area CV 0.038 vs 0.093; 10 and 20 fold). Chemotaxis unchanged (scale 3.54, saturation 105). At kappa = 8 the small sheet now collapses completely (area 0). Earlier calibration (2026-10-28, overlay immune layer):   REVISED per the 2026-10-28 vertex-mechanics review. Both substrates' mechanics are now DEFINED term by term (docs/mechanics.md). Every vertex parameter is either energy-matched to its CPM counterpart (area stiffness K = 2 lambda_volume, per cell type), lowered per type PAIR from the blueprint adhesion table (Lambda_ab = kappa * J_ab, ratios fixed by J), or CALIBRATED to measured CPM behaviour on the Sego initial state, under a hard mesh-validity constraint (no folded faces). With per-pair junction tension actually applied and auto_reconnect ON, the tension scale IS identifiable from mean cell area: kappa = 1.74 gives area 22.8 vs CPM 23.0. Immune random-walk displacement (9.4 vs 9.4 um) and the saturating chemotactic drift curve are matched. NOT matched: epithelial wandering. The CPM-matching motility folds the vertex mesh, so it is capped at the largest fold-free value and the vertex epithelium wanders about 5x less (MSD 2.0 vs 9.5 um^2), though it does exchange neighbours (T1s). Area dispersion is not matched either (CV 0.033 vs 0.093), and the kappa that fits the small isolated sheet differs (~4).

derived.insight: SUPERSEDED (2026-10-28): the earlier "tension non-identifiable" result came from the vertex backend collapsing the per-pair table to one mean tension and running only 6 steps.

studies.name: bp-01-blueprint-schema
studies.title: BP-01 — the blueprint as a versioned, backend-neutral artifact
studies.question: Can the biological blueprint be specified as a versioned, backend-neutral, statically-validated artifact, independent of CPM/vertex implementations?

findings.statement: One versioned canonical blueprint compiles unchanged to all three backends (CPM, vertex, center-based); backend/run parameters are separated into CompileOptions and flagged by a static validator; three worked examples validate and compile on every backend.

evidence.observed: 9 BP-01 acceptance tests pass; sego + mechanics_divergence validate contract-clean; 174 passed overall

findings.explanation: A canonical schema + split + validator make the biological blueprint a first-class, tested artifact.
findings.next_action: Stage 2 / BP-02: prove round-trip geometric fidelity (area, footprint, contact, adjacency, topology) with explicit error measures.

studies.claim: Stage 1 / BP-01 of the review program. The canonical blueprint is now a VERSIONED, backend-neutral artifact with a checked contract and a static validator -- the first of the three claims (blueprint fidelity) made a first-class, tested object rather than an implicit input. Specifically: (a) a `blueprint_version` field + versioned JSON schema; (b) a canonical/backend split (CompileOptions) so backend/run parameters (tension_scale, rules_seed) are kept OUT of the canonical biological state and recorded separately; (c) a static validator (`validate_blueprint` + `multicell-blueprint validate`) that reports structured diagnostics (errors AND contract warnings), not a success badge; (d) three hand-authored worked examples that validate and compile identically to BOTH backends.

derived.insight: One versioned canonical blueprint compiles unchanged to all three backends (CPM, vertex, center-based); backend/run parameters are separated into CompileOptions and flagged by a static validator; three worked examples validate and compile on every backend.

studies.name: initial-state-fidelity
studies.question: Do both substrates faithfully reproduce the blueprint's initial centroids, sizes and types, with one vertex polygon per blueprint cell?

findings.statement: The blueprint's t0 state materializes faithfully on all three backends (CPM exact; vertex one-hexagon-per-cell with a 1.6 um sub-cell epithelial residual; center-based one area-matched disc per cell at its centroid), so the cross-paradigm comparison begins from a shared initial condition.

evidence.observed: 48/48 type match; CPM RMS 0.000 um; vertex 36 hexagons (area 25) + 12 overlay, 0 guard, sheet RMS 1.60 um

findings.explanation: CPM seeds cells 1:1; vertex assigns cells 1:1 to a hexagonal lattice of the target area.

studies.claim: REVISED 2026-11-05: the vertex t0 is now ONE sheet of 48 hexagons (36 epithelial + 12 latent immune), the immune cells attached at the tissue margin site nearest their centroid instead of sitting as overlay islands on it. Epithelial centroid residual unchanged (rms 1.60, max 2.44 um); the immune cells move up to one cell diameter onto the margin (rms 4.11, max 5.60 um), closing the CPM's medium gap. All 48 cells present, types exact. Earlier reading (2026-10-28):   REVISED per the 2026-10-28 vertex-mechanics review. Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state (every cell's centroid, size and type), with every vertex polygon corresponding to exactly ONE Sego cell. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0). The vertex epithelium is a regular HEXAGONAL sheet at the target area (36 hexagons, area 25.0 each) mapped 1:1 onto the blueprint cells (sub-cell residual: RMS 1.60 um, max 2.44 um). The 12 immune cells are overlay islands exactly on their centroids, and the fields are overlaid on the tissue rather than meshed: no guard-ring or medium polygons remain.

derived.insight: The blueprint's t0 state materializes faithfully on all three backends (CPM exact; vertex one-hexagon-per-cell with a 1.6 um sub-cell epithelial residual; center-based one area-matched disc per cell at its centroid), so the cross-paradigm comparison begins from a shared initial condition.

studies.name: flu-lung-crossparadigm
studies.question: Does one backend-neutral blueprint reproduce the Sego 2022 influenza model on two different mechanical substrates, and -- judged against same-backend seed noise -- do the substrates diverge?

findings.statement: On the revised vertex substrate with mechanics-stochastic replicates, cross-backend fate agreement (0.938), infected-patch occupancy IoU (0.135) and patch location (3.6 um) all lie within the same-backend baselines (0.926/0.944; 0.100/0.175; 3.3 um), so we fail to reject a substrate difference on any of them.

evidence.observed: N=400: fate cross 0.938 vs same CPM 0.926 / vertex 0.944; IoU cross 0.135 vs 0.100 / 0.175; centroid 3.60 vs 3.33 um; area ratio 0.94; N=150 cross 0.987 vs same 0.976

findings.explanation: Fate is computed by the shared mechanism; the substrate enters only via field sampling + contact surface.
findings.next_action: more seeds + larger scale; Stage 4 producers (V/L/C/F)

findings.statement: The vertex I-count stays inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 100% of steps to N=150 but only 55% by N=400 -- a candidate late-dynamics substrate signal, not yet separated from the narrowness of a 3-seed envelope.

evidence.observed: vertex in-band 0.551 at N=400, 1.0 at N=150

findings.explanation: Infection spread later in the run may depend on each substrate's cell motility and contact geometry.
findings.next_action: widen the envelope with more CPM seeds; compare against a vertex-seed envelope

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED (2026-10-28, revised vertex substrate). On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross fate 0.942 vs CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um; vertex 100% inside the CPM envelope), so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate difference -- a null result, not proof of equality.

evidence.observed: cross 0.942 (0.890-1.000) vs same-backend CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; vertex in-band 1.0; N=150 cross == same == 0.987

expected.range: cross within the same-backend seed spread (null control)

findings.next_action: drive the ODE V/L/C/F producers (Task 21) and re-test at larger scale / more vertex seeds, where a substrate effect could become detectable

It is NOT a representation artifact (final mean areas match: CPM 24.67 vs vertex 24.51), so it is flagged as a CANDIDATE weak substrate signal -- not attributed to seed noise, which is untested -- to be checked at larger scale / more seeds.

findings.explanation: Faithful rates + reduced scale + producer-less ODE inputs -> weak drive; not tuned up (anti-goal).
findings.next_action: add the V/L/C/F producers and/or run longer; keep rates faithful

Vertex cells now move within the tissue and exchange neighbours, though the epithelium wanders ~5x less than on the CPM. Against that null, cell FATE, infected-patch OCCUPANCY and patch LOCATION all fall inside the same-backend seed spread (fail to reject). The one candidate substrate signal left: the vertex I-count leaves the narrow CPM 3-seed envelope for ~45% of steps by N=400.

studies.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
studies.question: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?

findings.statement: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 1->7 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.
findings.explanation: More seed virus raises the shared-field infection probability everywhere; the substrate sets only the noisy magnitude.
findings.next_action: revisit magnitudes once the ODE V producer lands (Task 21)

studies.name: crossparadigm-equivalence
studies.title: Backend equivalence (TOST)
studies.question: Are CPM and vertex EQUIVALENT (not merely "not-distinguishable") under replication -- and on which outcome: cell fate, exact spatial position, or both?

findings.statement: On the revised vertex substrate with mechanics-stochastic replicates, cross-backend fate agreement remains equivalent to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 (run-cluster diff -0.0014, 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008]).
findings.explanation: Fate is driven by the shared field/rule/ODE mechanism, identical across backends.

findings.statement: Exact-position agreement gap shrank from 0.92 to 0.135 (cluster CI [0.071, 0.210]): still not equivalent at +/-0.10. Most of the old gap was a degenerate null (identical mechanics across replicates) plus non-moving vertex cells; the rest tracks the vertex epithelium's lower fluidity.

evidence.observed: spatial same 0.608, cross 0.472; median displacement cross 5.7 / same CPM 5.2 / same vertex 2.3 um

findings.explanation: Immune motility and chemotaxis are calibrated, but the vertex epithelium is capped below CPM fluidity to keep the mesh valid.
findings.next_action: a fold-aware vertex topology handler to raise epithelial fluidity; scale-aware spatial descriptors (BP-06)

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED by F3 (2026-10-28 re-run; same conclusion). Cross-backend fate agreement is EQUIVALENT to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 under a DEPENDENCE-AWARE run-cluster bootstrap (diff -0.0015, 90% CI [-0.003,+0.001]; resampling the 6+6 runs, not the dependent pairs). The margin is not yet biologically justified and the CI is tight mainly because between-run variance is low at this scale. The pair-level p=5.6e-36 is retired as overstated.

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED by F4 (2026-10-28): the 1.00 same-backend baseline was an artifact of mechanically deterministic replicates. Exact cell POSITION is NOT backend-equivalent: cross-backend spatial agreement is 1.0 at t0 but 0.08 at the final frame (median drift ~8.5 um), while fate and final areas match. The capstone's "candidate IoU signal" is this representation drift -- the substrate changes where cells sit, not what they become.

findings.explanation: CPM lattice Metropolis and vertex tension relaxation move cell centroids along different paths even when fate is identical.

studies.name: substrate-divergence-counterfactual
studies.title: Mechanics-dominated counterfactual (positive control)
studies.question: When MECHANICS (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome, does the equivalence test correctly REJECT -- i.e. does it have the power to detect a real substrate difference?

findings.statement: On the calibrated vertex substrate with stochastic replicates, the spatial TOST still rejects (cross 0.417 vs same 0.775, diff +0.358), but not because of directed migration: neither substrate moves type A far up the gradient.

evidence.observed: spatial same 0.775, cross 0.417; A mean y CPM 11.0 -> 11.0, vertex 10.7 -> 10.1; N=80, seeds {0,1,2}

findings.explanation: Differential-adhesion sorting / positional dynamics differ between lattice Metropolis and vertex T1 rearrangement; not yet isolated.
findings.next_action: sweep adhesion contrast and gradient strength to map where equivalence breaks (BP-06/BP-07)

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED by F2 (2026-10-28): the vertex up-gradient climb was produced by the old, uncalibrated linear ActiveMigration mapping. In a mechanics-dominated regime the spatial equivalence TOST REJECTS (cross 0.20 vs same 1.00, diff +0.80 vs margin 0.10), driven by a directed migration difference (vertex A to y~17.9, CPM A to y~10.7). The equivalence test can detect a real substrate difference, so crossparadigm-equivalence's positive verdict is informative, not an insensitivity artifact.

evidence.observed: spatial same 1.000, cross 0.200; type-A mean final y cpm 10.7 vs vertex 17.9 (start 7); N=80, seeds {0,1,2}

findings.explanation: Vertex ActiveMigration climbs the field gradient; CPM Metropolis chemotaxis barely moves cells at this strength, and Potts sorting differs from vertex topology.
findings.next_action: none -- serves as the positive control; could be swept over gradient strength to map where equivalence breaks.
